name: Data Integrity for Manufacturing AI
title: Data Integrity for Manufacturing AI
answer: Data used to train and run manufacturing AI must meet the same integrity standards as other GMP data: attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate. The FDA's data integrity guidance applies to the records AI systems create and use.

reading.body:
Manufacturing AI inherits GMP data integrity rules: the records it trains on and produces must be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate.

The FDA's data integrity guidance, finalized in December 2018, was written for drug CGMP compliance, not for machine learning. The ALCOA principles it codifies are record properties, and they apply to a training set whenever the model built from it supports a quality decision. That reclassification is the whole point. A dataset stops being an engineering artifact and becomes a regulated record, which means version control, audit trails, and retention rules attach to it the way they attach to a batch record.

For AI specifically, the constraint lands on the data pipeline rather than the model. Attributable and contemporaneous records require knowing who produced each input and when, which is exactly what ad hoc scraping and unlogged preprocessing destroy. Teams that treat training data as disposable will fail an inspection that treats it as evidence.

The data here covers one guidance and one principle set. It does not say how the FDA has applied the guidance to a specific AI system, what enforcement has looked like, or how validation of the model itself differs from integrity of its inputs. Those are separate questions, and this material does not answer them.

sections.body: Training data sets are GMP records when the model supports quality decisions; control them accordingly.
